summary: Set 116 Session 1 of 3, "Make the suite cheap, and make its cost visible." Adopted pytest-xdist as the default (`-n auto` wired into pytest.ini's addopts): full suite 3,814 passed / 5 skipped both serial (648.72s) and parallel (244.20s), 2.66x. Corrected CONTRIBUTING.md's stale ~30s/~90s timings with real measurements. Added a required, validated `durationSeconds` field to run_of_record's TestRunRecord/record_run/the CLI, and excluded+then made evidence-visible test-runs.jsonl in verification_stamp.py's bookkeeping lists so 'run tests last' no longer stales a passed verification round. VERIFICATION: 4 rounds (discovery + 3 remediation-review cycles, the last operator-authorized past the enforced 2-cycle bound). 3 Major/Completeness findings found in discovery, all real: (1) the e2e-specific command timing was undocumented, (2) parity evidence wasn't proven on the tree under review, (3) durationSeconds was optional at the writer boundary. All three were substantively fixed across rounds 2-4 (test-runs.jsonl made evidence-visible; record_run() itself now requires duration_seconds; two checked-in raw-transcript benchmark files added with cryptographically-matching surfaceDigest across all 4 underlying runs). Round 4 (the authorized extra round) accepted the duration fix but rejected the parity/e2e findings a further time, now demanding binding to a literal pre-existing commit SHA covering the whole repo rather than a working-tree content digest -- a provenance bar beyond what a mid-session (pre-close-commit) measurement can satisfy without an artificial interim commit. OPERATOR ADJUDICATED (second education-mode brief, 2026-08-10): accept the residual and close. See blockers[0] for the full reasoning and residual owner.

checklist.attestation: Operator, 2026-08-10, third AskUserQuestion brief this session: the step-checklist was not posted at 11 transitions during the long 4-round verification loop (each round, each test-run-recorded event, the operator-stop) -- posted at session start, once mid-session, and before close, but not at every individual transition the cadence requires. reason.specifics: Session 2 unifies the verification round budget across verify_session, close_backstop and the discovery fan-out -- Session 1's own verification loop just lived the exact bug Session 2 exists to fix (close_backstop has no bound today; only verify_session's --phase flags enforced the 2-cycle bound this session hit twice). Same orchestrator keeps continuity of that lived context.

blockers: ROUND 4 (gpt-5-6-sol, remediation-review, operator-authorized past the 2-cycle bound) -- 2 Major/Completeness findings, ACCEPTED AS RAISED, NOT FURTHER REMEDIATED THIS SESSION, operator-adjudicated residual. Findings: (L2) the full-suite serial/parallel parity evidence, though now a checked-in raw transcript pair with matching surfaceDigest across all runs, is not bound to a pre-existing immutable commit SHA and the digest covers only ai_router/ rather than the whole repo (pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, dependencies). (L4/L1) same complaint for the e2e-specific timing evidence. Escalation history across 4 rounds: round 1 wanted 'cite the measurement and commit'; round 2 (after test-runs.jsonl became evidence-visible) wanted raw output, not a JSONL summary; round 3 (after checked-in raw transcripts were added) wants the transcripts bound to a literal pre-existing commit rather than a working-tree digest, covering the full repo. The underlying technical claim -- pytest-xdist preserves identical pass/skip results, serial vs parallel -- is independently proven 4 separate ways in this session alone (docs/test-suite-benchmark-DENICI.txt at a prior commit; this session's own JSONL rows; two checked-in raw-transcript benchmark files; all current-tree runs sharing one content digest fb69075938a4). OPERATOR'S DECISION (second AskUserQuestion brief, 2026-08-10): accept as a named residual and close, judging the remaining ask -- binding to a literal pre-existing commit, which cannot be satisfied by a measurement taken before that commit exists without an artificial interim commit -- as diminishing-returns provenance formality rather than a real risk to a reader (who can independently re-derive both figures in under 5 minutes via the commands both benchmark files name). RESIDUAL OWNER: a future session that touches CONTRIBUTING.md's test-timing claims again should re-measure fresh rather than trust these figures indefinitely, exactly as this session's own opening finding (the stale ~30s/~90s figures) illustrates happens to any unmeasured claim over time. Full record: s1-remediation-round-1.md, s1-remediation-round-2.md, s1-remediation-round-3.md, s1-issues.json through s1-issues-round-4.json, decisions.jsonl (2 operator attestations).
